about: The journey catalogue: every fixed sentence the agent says in English (the source), grouped domain > journey > step, plus languages, business settings and short prompt parts. Other languages: languages/<code>.json. Long prompts: prompts/*.md. See README.md.

languages.name: English
languages.style: Plain spoken English: short sentences, everyday words.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.style: Everyday spoken Hindi in Devanagari, the way people talk today. Keep common banking words in English as people say them (अकाउंट, बैलेंस, चार्ज, मिनिमम बैलेंस, डेबिट कार्ड, पेमेंट, ट्रांज़ैक्शन, EMI, FD, OTP), never bookish words (not शुल्क, रख-रखाव, आवश्यकता, न्यूनतम, लेनदेन, भुगतान).

languages.name: Hinglish
languages.style: Conversational Hindi written in Latin letters, mixed with English words the way callers speak.

core.refuse.text: I'm sorry, I don't have the details on that one. I can connect you to a colleague who can help. Shall I?

core.partial.text: I'd rather not guess the rest without checking, so I'll leave it there. Is there something specific you'd like to know?
core.partial.note: a later sentence failed its check: what was said stands, the rest is not guessed

core.more_kb.text: That's the main part. Would you like more detail on any of it?
core.more_kb.note: a long answer is stopped after a few sentences

core.partial_refer.text: I can't confirm the rest of that, so I'd rather not guess. I can connect you to a specialist. Shall I?
core.partial_refer.note: nothing usable was said before the check failed

core.conflict.text: I'm seeing two different figures for that, and I don't want to give you a wrong number. A specialist can confirm the right one for you. Shall I connect you?
core.conflict.note: two approved figures for exactly the same thing: never pick one

core.needs_verification.text: That needs your account details, so I'll first need to verify it's you. Please call from your registered mobile number, or I can connect you to our team.

core.handoff.text: Sure, I'll connect you to someone from our team.

core.smalltalk.text: Hi! I'm AU Bank's assistant, happy to help. You can ask me about your accounts, cards, deposits or loans.

core.charges_which.text: Sure. Would you like me to check the charges taken from your account, or would you like to know our general charges, like minimum balance, debit card or ATM charges?
core.charges_which.note: decided in code: a charges question that names no charge type, product or reason

core.variant_clarify.text: That depends on which one. We have {n} {family}, like {list}. Do you already have one with us, or are you thinking of getting one?
core.variant_clarify.note: decided in code: a generic question whose best passages belong to particular variants

core.out_of_scope.text: I can only help with AU Small Finance Bank's products and services.

core.code_by_keypad.text: Please enter the code on your keypad instead of saying it, and I won't hear it.

core.context_passed.text: No, I've passed on everything we discussed, so you won't need to repeat it. Please stay on the line.

core.ticket_status.text: Yes, it's registered. Your reference number is {ref}.

core.bare_yes.text: Sorry, which one do you mean? Please tell me in a few words.

core.auth_ack.text: Sure. Before I share your {what}, I need to verify it's you.
core.auth_ack.note: Said before the code when the caller asked about their own data: why verification is needed (PM review, 17 Nov).

core.otp_sent.text: For your security, I need to verify it's you. I've sent an OTP to your registered mobile number ending {last4}. Please enter it on your keypad.
core.otp_sent.note: "OTP", not "6-digit code": a voice read "6-digit" as "six dash digit" (Sarvam, 16 Nov).

core.otp_code.text: I've sent an OTP to your registered mobile number ending {last4}. Please enter it on your keypad.

core.need_mobile.text: For your security I need to verify you first. Please tell me your registered mobile number.

core.not_registered.text: That number isn't registered with us. Please tell me the mobile number registered with your account.

core.locked.text: I'm sorry, I'm not able to verify you on this call. Our team can help you another way. Shall I connect you?

core.fraud_first.text: Thanks for telling me. Let's make sure your account is safe.
core.fraud_first.note: The first line of a fraud report fits what happened (said once per call; the journey does not repeat it).

core.fraud_open_otp_shared.text: Okay, let's secure your account first.

core.fraud_open_unrecognised_debit.text: Let's look into that payment right away.

core.fraud_open_lost_card.text: Okay, let's make sure nobody can use that card.

core.fraud_team_option.text: If you'd rather speak to our fraud team straight away, just say so.

core.otp_invalid.text: That code didn't match. Please try again. You have {left} more {tries}.

core.unavailable.text: Sorry, I'm having trouble getting that right now. Please try again in a moment, or I can connect you to our team.

core.already_verified.text: You're already verified. Go ahead with your question.

core.no_code.text: There's no code waiting right now. Ask me your question and I'll send one if it's needed.

core.otp_expired.text: That code has expired. Ask me to send a new one.

core.action_unavailable.text: To make changes on your account I first need to verify it's you. Please call from your registered mobile number, or I can connect you to our team.

core.issue.text: I'm sorry about that. I'll connect you to our team so they can look into it right away.

journey.which_setting.text: Which setting would you like me to change on your card: online, shop, tap-to-pay, ATM or international payments?

journey.pos_still_off.text: And about the card not working at shops: shop payments are still switched off on it.

journey.cancelled.text: No problem, I won't. Is there anything else I can help you with?

journey.offer_transfer.text: I can connect you to our {dept} team. Shall I?

journey.ask_transfer.text: Of course. I'll connect you to our {dept} team. Is that okay?

journey.ask_transfer_rm.text: Of course. I'll connect you to our Priority Banking team, where your relationship manager {rm} sits. Is that okay?

journey.connecting.text: Connecting you to our {dept} team now. I've shared what we discussed, so you won't need to repeat it. Please stay on the line.

journey.after_hours.text: Our {dept} team is available from {hours}, so I've booked a callback for you instead. Your reference is {ref}, and they'll call you on your registered number.

journey.not_allowed.text: That's not something I can do on this call, but our {dept} team can help you with it. Shall I connect you?

journey.fraud_recent.text: These are your latest debits: {list}. Is it one of these?

journey.fraud_no_recent.text: I don't see any debits in the last seven days. Roughly when did it happen, and how much was it? If you feel your account isn't safe, I can connect you to our fraud team right away.
journey.fraud_no_recent.note: PM review, 17 Nov: no recent debit must not sound like "all is well"; a person is offered at once

journey.otp_recent.text: Here's what went out in the last two days: {list}.

journey.otp_none.text: I don't see any payments from your account in the last two days, but a shared code can also be used to log in or add a payee, so your account needs to be secured now.
journey.otp_none.note: A shared code is used for more than payments (logins, new payees, UPI set-up): no payment is not "good news"

journey.otp_next.text: Please don't share it with anyone again. The bank never asks for it. To be safe, I'd like to connect you to our fraud team now so they can secure your net banking, UPI and cards. Shall I?

journey.lead_offer_apply.text: Would you like someone from our team to call you and help you apply?

journey.fraud_txn.text: a payment of ₹{amt} at {who} on {date} on your {card}

journey.fraud_followup.text: Shall I also raise a dispute for {what} and connect you to our fraud team, so they can take it forward?

journey.fraud_followup_generic.text: Shall I connect you to our fraud team now, so they can check your recent transactions with you?

journey.replacement_yes.text: Yes. With a permanent block, a replacement card is sent to your registered address.

journey.replacement_temp.text: No. A temporary block keeps the same card, so you can unblock it later. A new card comes only with a permanent block.

journey.action_scheduled_no.text: I can't schedule that for later. I can unblock it right now, or you can call us tomorrow and it will be done on the call. Would you like me to unblock it now?
journey.action_scheduled_no.note: "unblock it tomorrow at 10": a later unblock cannot be booked; said plainly, nothing is scheduled or done

journey.block_type_q.text: Would you like to block your card temporarily, so you can unblock it later, or permanently, with a replacement card sent to you?

journey.block_type_again.text: Sorry, should I block it temporarily or permanently?

journey.open_request.text: By the way, I can see you have an open {kind} with us about {topic}. Is today's call about that?

journey.fraud_none.text: I couldn't find a payment like that in your recent activity. Could you tell me roughly when it happened, which account or card, and who it was paid to?

journey.fraud_many.text: I can see {n} payments that could be it: {list}. Which one is it?

journey.fraud_pending.text: It's still showing as processing. Since you don't recognise it, it's best to report it now.
journey.fraud_pending.note: The status as the bank shows it, never a guess about how it ends ("may be reversed by itself" invited waiting)

journey.fraud_reversed.text: That payment was reversed, so the money is back in your account. If there's another one you don't recognise, tell me.

journey.fraud_upi_followup.text: Shall I raise a fraud complaint for it and connect you to our fraud team? You can also report it on the cyber crime helpline, 1930.

journey.fraud_bank_down.text: I'm sorry, I can't check your account right now, and I don't want you to wait. I can connect you to our fraud team straight away. Shall I?

journey.lost_recent.text: I can see {n} recent payments on that card, the latest ₹{amt} at {who}. If any of them isn't yours, I can raise a dispute and connect you to our fraud team. Shall I?

journey.lost_none.text: I don't see any recent payments on that card. Shall I connect you to our fraud team, in case you want them to check anything else?

journey.fraud_advice.text: Please don't share your OTP, PIN or CVV with anyone. You can also report it to the cyber crime helpline on 1930.

journey.already_blocked.text: Your {card} is already blocked, so it can't be used.

journey.issue_details.text: I'm sorry about that. Let me look into it. Roughly how much was it, and when did it happen?

journey.offer_ticket.text: Would you like me to raise a {kind} with our {dept} team? They'll get back to you by {date}.

journey.ticket_done.text: Done. I've raised it, and your reference number is {ref}. Our {dept} team will get back to you by {date}.

journey.txn_not_found.text: I couldn't find a transaction like that in your recent activity.

journey.lead_offer.text: Would you like someone from our team to call you to help you open it?

journey.lead_done.text: Lovely. Someone from our team will call you on this number by {date}. Your reference is {ref}. You can also open a Digital account yourself in the AU 0101 app with a quick video KYC.

journey.lead_no_number.text: You can open a Digital account yourself in the AU 0101 app with a quick video KYC, or visit any AU branch.

journey.busy_callback.text: I'm sorry for the wait. Everyone in our {dept} team is busy right now. I've booked a callback for you, reference {ref}, and they'll call you on your registered number by {date}. Thank you for calling AU Bank.

journey.fraud_side_q.text: I can't confirm that from here. The fraud team can check it with you.
journey.fraud_side_q.note: Regression pack, 17 Nov: a side question or a detail while a fraud offer waits keeps the offer (it used to be dropped, the payment forgotten, and "yes, raise a complaint" re-listed debits). Answers never promise an outcome.

journey.fraud_context.text: No, I'll pass on everything we've discussed, so you won't need to repeat it.

journey.fraud_noted.text: Thank you, I'll pass that on to the fraud team.

journey.fraud_restate_ticket.text: Shall I raise the complaint and connect you to them now?

journey.fraud_restate.text: Shall I connect you to them now?

journey.fraud_pick_more.text: That's okay. Do you remember roughly how much it was, or whether it was by UPI, card or ATM? If you'd rather, I can connect you to our fraud team now.

journey.fraud_safe_q.text: I can't confirm that from the transactions alone. If you think someone has used your account, I can connect you to our fraud team right away. Shall I?

journey.lost_no_block.text: All right, I won't block it. While the card is out of your hands, someone could still use it, so our fraud team should look at other ways to protect you. Shall I connect you to them now?
journey.lost_no_block.note: "my card is stolen, but don't block it": no block is offered; the risk is said and the fraud team offered

journey.action_later_unblock.text: Yes. It stays blocked until you ask us to unblock it. Just call us when you're ready and it can be done on the call.
journey.action_later_unblock.note: "can I unblock it tomorrow?" is a question about later, not an order to do it now

journey.action_later.text: Yes, you can. Just call us when you're ready and it can be done on the call.

journey.restate_transfer.text: I'd connect you to our {dept} team, who handle {what}. Shall I go ahead?

bank.total_scope.text: No. That total is only money you paid out. Money people sent you isn't included.

bank.pending_none.text: I don't see any pending payment on your accounts right now.

bank.txn_each_overview.text: I'll go through your {n} accounts one at a time, starting with the account ending {l4}.

bank.txn_each_intro.text: On your account ending {l4}, here are the last {k}.

strategy.direct: Answer exactly the detail asked, in one to three short sentences.
strategy.product_overview: Broad question about one product: in 40 to 65 words say what it is and who it suits, its two or three most useful benefits and its main fee. Leave the rest out, then offer to go into one part (for a card: rewards, fees or eligibility).
strategy.full: The caller asked for the full details: cover every point they asked for in short spoken sentences, in a natural order, without skipping conditions.
strategy.compare: Compare the products the caller named, side by side on the points that matter most to them (fee, main benefit, who it suits), in short spoken sentences. Cover every named product that has a source; never describe one that has no source.
strategy.overview: The caller wants the whole picture: give a short spoken overview - the range from lowest to highest and at most three examples - then ask which one they are interested in.
strategy.recommend: Recommend one or two products from the sources that fit the caller's needs, each with one short reason, and mention the main eligibility condition if the sources give one. Do not list every option. End by asking if they'd like to know more about one of them.

language.hi: reply in everyday spoken Hindi, in Devanagari script, the way people talk today: keep common banking words in English as people say them (अकाउंट, बैलेंस, चार्ज, मिनिमम बैलेंस, डेबिट कार्ड, पेमेंट, ट्रांज़ैक्शन, EMI, FD), never bookish words (not शुल्क, रख-रखाव, आवश्यकता, न्यूनतम, लेनदेन, भुगतान); keep product names and numbers exactly as written
language.hinglish: reply in Hinglish - conversational Hindi written in Latin script mixed with English, like the caller
